niche: a state lodging association's 2027 Rising Destinations co-op marketing match, a fixed fund split across the counties whose taxable lodging receipts grew at least five per cent from 2024 to 2025 in proportion to their 2025 receipts, where 2025 must be restated from the association's fixed monthly member panel onto the Department of Revenue's annual county basis a year before the Department publishes it

analyst_test: With every report extracted and every file conformed, the easy route carries each county's 2024 Department receipts forward by its member panel's 2024 to 2025 growth (the same as scaling the panel by its 2024 ratio to the Department) and qualifies the counties whose member hotels grew five per cent or more; but in every year since the panel was drawn the Department's receipts outgrew the panel's by a steady margin that differs by county, and adding a year of that margin qualifies counties the easy route leaves out and moves the match.
domain_test: Benchmarking a sub-annual indicator to annual benchmarks and extrapolating past the last benchmark on the path of the benchmark-to-indicator ratio, the way official time-series production carries a monthly survey past its latest annual census (the IMF Quarterly National Accounts Manual's chapter on benchmarking); with another field's nouns there is no sample panel that misses the whole's new entrants and no lagged complete count to benchmark it to, so the step does not exist.
layer2_pattern: own:benchmark-to-indicator ratio extrapolated on its own path past the last benchmark

world.geography: United States (a fictional state's sixteen counties)
world.org_type: state lodging association, a member trade body

driver: A total for a period not yet counted is carried from the last complete count by the movement of a fixed sample, and the sample covers a shrinking share of the whole because new members join only the whole, at a pace that differs by area and has held steady through every counted period; carrying the last count by the sample's movement, or scaling the sample by the last count's ratio to it, drops one more period of that drift, so the ratio must be carried forward on its own path.
driver_concrete: The association's member panel was fixed when it was drawn, so hotels opened since then reach the Department's receipts and never the panel, and in the counties where hotels keep opening the Department's receipts have outgrown the panel's by a steady few points every year; moving 2024's receipts by the panel's 2025 growth leaves that year's margin out and ranks the counties on member hotels' growth alone.
stump: The default path moves each county's 2024 Department receipts by its member panel's 2024 to 2025 growth, qualifies the counties whose member hotels grew five per cent or more and splits the match among them, because it never asks how the panel's growth has tracked the Department's in the years both are known.

differentiation.task123: task123 splits each unit's interval total onto calendar periods by a daily-measured sample's within-interval rate; here no interval is split: a fixed sample's annual movement is carried past the last complete count on the path of its ratio to that count.
differentiation.task474: task474 carries short counts to a year by a calendar pattern measured at reference sites; here the reference is the lagged complete count itself and the move is the drift of the sample's coverage of it, year over year.
differentiation.task481: task481 restates a count onto a new classification by conversion rates from a dual-coded window; here nothing is reclassified: the same quantity is measured completely each year with a lag and by a fixed sample monthly, and the sample's shortfall grows.
differentiation.task133: task133 counts a taken-over loan's exposure only from the go-live, a risk set filled with months the record never watched; here no unit's exposure or outcome is counted: a fixed sample keeps losing share of a whole that gains members it never takes in, and the whole's lagged count shows the loss growing at a steady pace that is carried one year further.

lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-21 at stage 4: a reader landed the call by reading guidelines 3.1's 'would bring ... as they stand' literally and replaying each claim's water on the present floor; judge FIX_NOW on ask B
lineage.driver: A record of past events on units is carried to the units as they now stand, and some units were raised after their events, so a past event counts again on a raised unit only where the event's recorded level stood above the unit's new threshold; dropping a raised unit's earlier events, keeping them all, or giving it the later rate of units in its present class each misstates the expected rate.
lineage.stump: The default path drops every claim a building filed before it was elevated and puts the two riverine counties elevated after 2016 in the pilot, because it never asks whether the 2016 water would still have reached the raised floors.
lineage.niche: a regional flood authority's 2027 private flood placement pilot, set on each member county's expected paid building claims per 1,000 insured buildings for the buildings insured today as they now stand, built from the NFIP claims history, the policy terms and the authority's own elevation and acquisition projects, where the 2016 flood rose above the floors the post-flood elevations were built to
